prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A crop-by-crop season reference: compare when each crop is sown and harvested, what it yields, and any notes.","reading":"Primarily row-wise: fix the crop in col 1, read cols 2–3 as one sowing-to-harvest window, then col 4 yield and col 5 caveat; secondarily scan down the date columns to compare seasons.","groups":["col 1 is the row anchor","cols 2–3 are a paired timing unit and must stay adjacent","col 4 is the quantitative outcome","col 5 is free-text commentary attached to the whole row"],"keep_intact":["crop names in col 1","month/season names and date ranges in cols 2–3","yield numbers and the টন/হেক্টর unit in col 4","row identity"],"may_wrap":["date ranges at spaces and em dashes","the yield header between ফলন and (টন/হেক্টর)","parenthetical crop qualifiers","comments in col 5, which must wrap extensively"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 195] · table 525×999px · row heights [83, 176, 129, 153, 153, 153, 153] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 165px
Design r2B: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 250] · table 580×836px · row heights [83, 153, 106, 129, 129, 106, 129] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 220px
Design r2C: widths [90, 115, 110, 63, 185] · table 564×1069px · row heights [83, 176, 153, 176, 153, 153, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 204px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r2A","good":"All five columns are present and no word is split mid-glyph. Meanwhile the timing pair at 87/89px is barely a third of its one-line width, so sowing and harvest each run to four or five lines and stop reading as a single sowing→harvest window. Comments at 195px still clip at the dashed edge and reach seven lines; the table grows to 999px tall.","cause":"The width budget was spent on col 5 (195px) while col 4 was left pinned at its unbreakable-word floor of 63px. Cols 2–3 at 94 keep three-to-four-line date wraps, col 4 at 82 keeps yield values whole and its header at two lines, and col 5 is held at 260 — a deliberate compromise that keeps the total near 648px (less scrolling than core-fit) at the cost of five-line notes."}]}
